overview: Hepatitis E is an inflammation of the liver caused by infection with the hepatitis E virus. The virus is shed in the stools of infected people and enters the human body through the oral route. The infection is usually self-limiting and resolves within 2–6 weeks.
diagnosis: detection of specific anti-HEV immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibodies
elevated serum concentrations of alanine aminotransferase (ALT)
elevated serum concentrations of aspartate aminotransferase (AST)
treatment: avoidance of unnecessary medications that can adversely affect liver function
hospitalization for people with fulminant hepatitis
transmission: consumption of uncooked or undercooked meat
prevention: maintaining quality standards for public water supplies
vaccination (licensed in China and other countries)
risk_factors: organ transplant recipients on immunosuppressive drugs
complications: chronic hepatitis E infection in immunosuppressed people
key_facts: 3450 deaths and 19.47 million cases of acute hepatitis E globally in 2021
5.4% of global disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) related to acute hepatitis
20–25% of pregnant women can die if they get hepatitis E in the third trimester
